topics.label: Introduction and Overview of Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture objectives, reviewing the hallmarks of cancer and the progression model of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Signaling Pathways Driving Proliferation and Survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular receptor pathways, Wnt signaling, and downstream kinase cascades disrupt normal growth control to promote sustained proliferation.

topics.label: Differentiation Blocks in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to undergo terminal differentiation, using examples from hematological malignancies and intestinal epithelial stem cells.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Evading Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how alterations in p53 and the BAX–BCL2 balance prevent programmed cell death in cancer cells.

topics.label: Telomere Regulation, Senescence, and Stress Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere shortening drives cellular senescence, how telomerase activation bypasses replicative limits to immortalise tumor cells, and how p53 mediates overarching stress and genome-protection responses.

topics.label: Metabolic Rewiring and Oncometabolites in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic reprogramming, and the epigenetic impact of oncometabolites in cancer.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and the Angiogenic Switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers the requirement of blood vessel recruitment for tumor growth and the regulation of the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Determinants of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the sequential process of cancer dissemination, the seed-and-soil compatibility governing metastatic success, and the genomic features underlying metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, summarizing the convergence of diverse mutations onto common hallmarks.
